title: Co-design sprint blueprint and speaker notes
summary: Compact blueprint for a 3-hour co-design sprint with a mid-market customer evaluating Redwood Dedicated. Designed to drive a deployment decision by aligning stakeholders on acceptance criteria, integration constraints, and a minimal viable rollout plan. Includes slide-by-slide skeleton, facilitator prompts, prework checklist and next-step playbook.
prework: (send 5 days before) 1) Survey: team roles + success metrics (1 page). 2) Network diagram: customer to on-prem/VPC ingress path (rough sketch). 3) Example payloads (3 representative requests). 4) List of must-have security controls (KMS, audit, SOC/ISO requirements). Ask attendees to set calendar reminders for a 30-minute pre-brief with their infrastructure lead.
agenda:
Duration: 3 hours total

00:00–00:10 — Welcome & goal framing
  - Host: SE lead (Marceline) sets outcome: decision on POC scope and success metrics.
  - Quick round-robin: attendee name + one priority.

00:10–00:30 — Customer context lightning (product & infra owners)
  - Customer presents current infra, peak QPS needs, sensitive data flows.
  - SE captures constraints on whiteboard (network, compliance, latency).

00:30–01:00 — Live workload mapping exercise
  - Map three representative flows to Redwood deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
  - Facilitator prompt: "Which flows require data residency or KMS?"
  - Output: recommended deployment mode per flow.

01:00–01:20 — Break + small-group prep: risk and mitigations

01:20–02:00 — Architecture showdown and tradeoffs (interactive)
  - Present 3 candidate architectures (single-region dedicated, hybrid hosted + private, private-only).
  - For each: list cost/latency/operational tradeoffs.
  - Voting: stakeholders use dot-vote to record preferences.

02:00–02:25 — Success criteria workshop (define measurable POC gates)
  - Draft SLOs: P50/P95 latency, throughput, availability, cost per 1k tokens, functional accuracy on sample prompt set.
  - Agree on acceptance thresholds and measurement method.

02:25–02:45 — POC plan & roles (30 minute cadence to go-live)
  - Deliverables, owners, timeline (weeks 0–6), required infra tickets, support windows.
  - Quick checklist: data ingress, secrets, VPC peering, firewall rules, observability hooks.

02:45–03:00 — Next steps, decision, and close
  - Confirm go/no-go; assign immediate action items (POC kickoff calendar + pre-check run).
  - Capture parking-lot items and follow-up owners.
slide_outline:
Slide 1: Title + desired outcome (1 slide)
  - Speaker note: "Frame as decision-oriented session; deliver go/no-go by EOD on POC scope."
Slide 2: Agenda & rules of engagement (1 slide)
  - Note: call out decision owners up front.
Slide 3: Customer context snapshot (2 slides)
  - One slide for org & product; one slide for infra constraints and existing auth/KMS.
Slide 4: Example workload patterns (1 slide)
  - Show 3 representative payloads and expected QPS/latency.
Slide 5: Candidate architectures (3 slides — one per pattern)
  - Diagram + pros/cons + estimated cost band (low/med/high).
Slide 6: Tradeoff heatmap (1 slide)
  - Latency vs cost vs compliance requirements.
Slide 7: Measurable POC gates (1 slide)
  - P50/P95 targets, accuracy checks, pilot traffic plan.
Slide 8: Operational runbook checklist (1 slide)
  - Tickets to open, sample monitoring dashboards, escalation path.
Slide 9: Timeline & owners (1 slide)
  - Week-by-week milestones.
Slide 10: Risks & mitigations (1 slide)
  - Known blockers + mitigation owner.
Slide 11: Decision & next steps (1 slide)
  - Formalize go/no-go and immediate actions.
Slide 12: Appendix: sample prompts, test harness details, contact matrix (2 slides)
facilitator_notes:
Tone: pragmatic, decision-first, time-boxed. Encourage cross-functional voices (product, infra, security). Keep architecture discussions to 20 minutes per candidate. Use the following prompts during mapping exercise:
  - "What part of this flow contains PHI/PII?"
  - "If latency is 2x the target, can the UX accept graceful degradation?"
  - "Who owns egress charges for third-party APIs?"
  - "What is the rollback plan if model regression occurs after rollout?"

Time management: call out time checks at 25, 55, 80, 110 minutes. Be blunt about parking-lot items: capture and move on.

Decision rules (pre-agree with customer sponsor):
  - Executive sponsor can make final call when the core cross-functional group is present.
  - If any security control is a blocker, escalate to security lead within 48 hours.

Common friction and mitigation playbook:
  - Networking: request network diagram and sample firewall rule within 48 hours; offer a temporary tunneling option for POC.
  - Data residency: recommend dedicated/private option and outline encryption KMS options.
  - Cost concerns: show quick cost-estimate ranges and propose strict quota limits during POC.
  - Model quality/regression: propose a small, representative eval set and nightly regression checks; hold a gating call on failures.

Facilitator checklist (before workshop):
  - Confirm attendees and decision owner.
  - Verify prework received (payloads, network diagram, security constraints).
  - Deploy a minimal demo or recorded video of Redwood console flows to share.
  - Create Miro board (mapping + dot-vote) and pre-seed diagrams.

Follow-up template (send within 24 hours):
  - Summary of decisions and agreed POC gates.
  - Action items with owners + due dates.
  - Link to workshop Miro, slide deck, and onboarding playbook.
success_criteria:
POC acceptance gates (must be explicit and measurable):
  - Latency: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 400ms on representative payload set under test load.
  - Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent requests for 10 minutes without queue growth.
  - Cost: projected cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget band (+/- 25%).
  - Security: encryption-at-rest verified, KMS integration proof-of-concept, and logging to customer's SIEM.
  - Quality: >= 90% pass rate on sample prompt evaluation (customer-provided rubric).
  - Observability: traceable per-request latency and token breakdown visible in Redwood Console.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Customer network policy prevents inbound peering.
  - Mitigation: Offer outbound-only egress with VPN or temporary tunnel; estimate 3–5 business days.
Risk: Keys/KMS policy conflicts with our default KMS provider.
  - Mitigation: Plan for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) flow and schedule KMS integration in week 2.
Risk: Unexpected tokenization/encoding mismatch causing quality issues.
  - Mitigation: Include tokenizer diagnostic step in week 0 and run small regression harness.
next_steps_playbook:
1) Within 24 hours: send workshop notes + draft POC scope for review.
2) Within 3 business days: formalize PO, schedule infra pre-check, open necessary tickets (network, secrets).
3) Week 0: infra setup + smoke test (1–2 days).
4) Week 1–2: ingest sample traffic, run accuracy checks, tune batching/quantization settings.
5) Week 3–4: ramp traffic, monitor SLOs, run end-to-end failover tests.
6) Week 5–6: finalize runbook, cutover plan, and handoff to operations.
notes_to_self: Keep slide deck lean; append deep-dive logs in appendix. If customer pushes for hosted pricing, be ready with a hosted-to-dedicated migration cost delta. Ask solutions-ops to pre-provision a sandbox dedicated pool to shorten POC lead time. Capture any off-template asks as an addendum to the POC scope to avoid scope creep.
